headline: Kremlin Move on Kurils Sparks Japan's Outrage
deck: The Russian leader's first visit to the contested Pacific islands escalates a decades-old territorial dispute, threatening regional stability.
body: Vladimir Putin's inaugural visit to the disputed Kuril Islands drew immediate condemnation from Japan, reigniting long-standing tensions over the Pacific archipelago.
Tokyo swiftly launched a protest following the Russian president's arrival on Etorofu island, which lies off Hokkaido. This marks his first visit to the contested territory.
Japan's Prime Minister Takaichi labeled Putin's visit 'absolutely unacceptable,' underscoring the depth of Tokyo's diplomatic anger.
The Kuril Islands have been a source of contention between Japan and Russia since the close of World War II, when Soviet forces seized them from Japan.
Despite decades passing, the ownership of the Kuril Islands remains unresolved, serving as a persistent point of friction in bilateral relations.
This latest incident highlights the enduring geopolitical complexities of the region, signaling continued diplomatic challenges for both nations in resolving their territorial claims.
